ask: Should LangQuest get a USB backup of one person's own work first, or a full hand-over between people, or nothing yet?
problem: Translators often work offline for weeks. Their unsent recordings live only on the phone. A lost or broken phone loses that work. The issue has no text, so the goal of USB backup and import is not yet defined.
found: The server accepts each event once and checks its author, so an imported event is safe if it enters as unsent. The app cannot save files today. I found no trace of LAN-227's export in the repository.
changed: Nothing in the app. This pull request holds only this question and three pictures. Nothing is built until you answer.
why: Three real choices exist. Nothing keeps today's rules but leaves the lost-phone risk. A personal backup solves the lost-phone risk and is the smallest step. A hand-over between people helps teams with no internet, but it needs a new rule about who may carry whose work. Every option keeps the sync rules: imports arrive as unsent events, the server checks them, and audio files are never changed. I recommend the personal backup, with a file layout that lets a hand-over follow later.
touches: Option 2 and 3 add a file picker and sharing tool to the phone app. That changes the Play Store file answers and needs a new entry in the decision log. Option 3 also changes how sign-out hand-overs on shared phones work.

options.label: Build nothing yet
options.result: No change. Unsent work is still lost if a phone is lost or broken.

options.label: Personal backup and restore
options.result: A person saves their unsent work and recordings to a USB stick, then restores them on a new phone with the same sign-in. Restored work enters as unsent and the server checks it.

options.label: Hand-over between people
options.result: A courier carries a stick from an offline phone to an online one, which sends the work as its author. It needs a new permission rule and more testing.
